questions.prompt: This pilot light station runs its working program, but one input is wired wrong. Press **Button 1** alone, then **Button 2** alone, and watch the PB1 and PB2 contacts. Which fault does it have?
options: PB2's input is wired to Button 1: PB2 turns TRUE when Button 1 is pressed, and Button 2 does nothing
The wire to PB2 is broken: PB2 is always FALSE, so Button 2 does nothing and Amber never lights
PB2 is shorted: PB2 is always TRUE, so Amber is lit with nothing pressed and Button 2 changes nothing
The Amber light has failed: the PLC turns Amber on when Button 2 is pressed, but the lamp stays dark
questions.explanation: Button 1 alone lights Green and Amber, because PB1 and PB2 both turn TRUE. With nothing pressed PB2 is FALSE, so it is not a short; and Button 2 changes nothing, because no input is wired to it.

questions.prompt: This motor station runs its working program, but one input is faulty. Watch the machine from **Reset**, then hold **Stop** and let go. Which fault does it have?
options: The Start input is shorted: it is always TRUE, so the motor starts by itself
The Stop wire is broken: Stop is always FALSE, so the motor will not run
The Stop input is shorted: it is always TRUE, so Stop cannot stop the motor
The program has no seal-in: the motor runs only while Start is held down
questions.explanation: Start reads TRUE with nobody pressing it, so the motor runs from power-up. Stop stops it only while held; let go and Start, still TRUE, starts it again.

questions.prompt: This tank runs its working program, but one input is faulty. Turn the Mode switch to **Auto** and watch the tank rise past 80 %. Which fault does it have?
options: The high float's wire is broken: HighFloat stays FALSE when the liquid reaches it, and the tank overflows
The low float's wire is broken: LowFloat is always FALSE, so the pump never empties the tank
The fill valve has failed: it stays open after the PLC turns it off, and the tank overflows
The Auto switch's wire is broken: the PLC never sees Auto, so the tank never starts to fill
questions.explanation: The fill valve opens and the level rises, so Auto and the valve work. At 80 % What every part is doing says the high float senses the liquid, but HighFloat stays FALSE, so nothing stops the filling.

questions.prompt: This garage door runs its working program, but one input is faulty. Press **Open** and let the door open fully, press **Step into the doorway**, then press **Close**. Which fault does it have?
options: The safety eye's input is always TRUE (stuck clear, or shorted): the door comes down on what is in the doorway
The safety eye's wire is broken: EyeClear is always FALSE, so the door never closes at all
The bottom limit switch is shorted: it always reads TRUE, so the door stops as soon as it starts
The Close button is shorted: it always reads TRUE, so the door closes as soon as it is open
questions.explanation: EyeClear stays TRUE although something is in the beam, so the Down rung lets the door close on it. From the PLC, a stuck sensor and a shorted wire look the same: both read TRUE whatever happens.

questions.prompt: This sorter runs its working program, but one input is faulty. Press **Start** and watch rungs 2 and 3 as the first metal part passes the metal sensor and then the photo-eye. Which fault does it have?
options: The metal sensor's wire is broken: Prox never turns TRUE, so metal parts ride on to Bin B
The photo-eye's wire is broken: Eye never turns TRUE, so no part is ever diverted
The diverter has failed: the PLC turns Divert on for metal, but the arm does not move
The photo-eye is shorted: Eye is always TRUE, so metal parts are diverted too early
questions.explanation: What every part is doing says the metal sensor sees the metal part, but the Prox contact never turns TRUE and MetalSeen is never set. The photo-eye's contact does turn TRUE as each part passes, so the eye is fine.

questions.prompt: This reversing conveyor runs its working program, but one input is faulty. Press **Forward**, then hold **Stop**. Which fault does it have?
options: The Stop input is shorted: StopPB is always TRUE, so Stop never stops the motor
The Stop wire is broken: StopPB is always FALSE, so the motor never starts
The Forward button is shorted: it is always TRUE, so the motor starts again after Stop
The program has no interlock: Forward and Reverse can both be on at once
questions.explanation: StopPB stays TRUE while Stop is held down. This is the dangerous way for a Stop input to fail, and why an emergency stop is also wired straight into the power circuit.

questions.prompt: A photo-eye's input reads TRUE all the time, with nothing in front of it. From the PLC alone, can you tell a shorted wire from a sensor stuck ON?
options: No: both make the input TRUE. Look at the sensor's own light, or test the wire with a meter with the power safely isolated
Yes: a shorted wire always makes the PLC stop with a fault and show it, and a stuck sensor does not
Yes: a stuck sensor reads TRUE only every other scan, and a shorted wire reads TRUE in every scan
No, and it does not matter: both are fixed the same way, by changing the program to ignore it
questions.explanation: The PLC sees only the value at its terminal. Where the fault is, the sensor or the wire, is found at the machine.

questions.prompt: Match each input fault to what the PLC sees.

pairs.left: A broken wire on a normally closed Stop
pairs.right: As if Stop were held down

questions.explanation: A normally closed Stop reads TRUE while all is well, so a broken wire to it reads like a press: the machine fails safe.
